title: Event-driven fallbacks and policy runtime cleanup
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background:
The smart routing hotpath currently performs synchronous policy evaluation and fallback selection while holding cross-region locks and touching several shared caches. This pattern increases tail latency during bursts and complicates retries and rollbacks. We've also accumulated ad-hoc fallback heuristics in multiple places, making changes risky.

Goal:
1) Separate the policy runtime (side-effect-free scoring + decision surface) from the fallback coordinator that mutates routing state.
2) Replace the blocking fallback path with an event-driven coordinator that consumes capacity/latency events and reconciles fallback choices asynchronously.
3) Remove global mutable routing locks on the hotpath and replace them with optimistic reads + short-lived leases where needed.
4) Upgrade the in-process eventbus library to eventbus v2.1 and concurrency primitives to tokio-1.22 (see dependencies).

Acceptance criteria:
- No more global routing mutex held on the hotpath for >2ms under normal load.
- p95 tail latency for a 64-token generative request does not regress more than 5% in canary traffic.
- Under simulated burst, throughput (requests/s) of the routing service improves by >=10% versus baseline.
- Fallback decisions are auditable in the new fallback-events stream (event IDs persisted) and visible in Console.

Design summary / Implementation plan:
1) Policy runtime: extract scoring functions into a pure evaluation module (policy-eval) with a compact API (evaluate(context) -> candidate-scores). This module is safe to run on the hotpath without acquiring locks.
2) Fallback coordinator: new small service (or library component when running colocated) that subscribes to an internal event stream (capacity updates, latency spikes, health checks). It reconciles current routing table state to a desired state and emits minimal diffs to the routing cache. The coordinator will use an event-sourcing pattern so changes are idempotent.
3) Event delivery: adopt eventbus v2.1 for in-process fanout; for multi-node durability we write canonical events to the routing-events Kafka topic.
4) Locking: remove the global routing mutex; for short critical updates use a short lease via leader-election or per-shard optimistic compare-and-swap.
5) Feature flags: rollout behind console-configurable flags: routing.fallbacks.evented=true and routing.policy.runtime=v2 to allow safe rollback.

Risk & trade-offs:
- Asynchronous coordination increases time-to-propagation for fallback changes. Mitigation: coordinator supports fast-path synchronous fallback for critical capacity failures for the first 30 seconds after a major capacity shift.
- Eventual consistency can surface transient misroutes. Mitigation: monitor misroute rate and add transient-forwarding heuristics (forward request to next-best variant until coordinator converges).

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for policy-eval to cover boundary scoring logic and edge-cases.
- Integration test harness that replays historical capacity events (from incident dataset) against the coordinator to verify stability.
- Load test: run canary routing instances with production traffic replay and compare latency/throughput metrics.
- Chaos test: kill coordinator pod and validate graceful degradation to legacy synchronous fallback (toggle by FF).

Metrics & dashboards:
- New metrics: fallback_event_latency_ms, fallback_convergence_time_ms, fallback_audit_rate, misroute_rate_by_region.
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd-routing/fallbacks-overview (canary panel added).

Release & rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (dev): library refactor and unit tests, internal integration test using local eventbus (2 weeks).
- Phase 2 (canary): enable evented fallbacks on low-traffic customer shard (10% traffic), observe metrics for 72 hours.
- Phase 3 (gradual): 25% -> 50% -> 100% in weekly increments if metrics are green.
- Rollback: flip routing.fallbacks.evented=false and fall back to v1 synchronous path; coordinator writes a compensating event to revert any state diffs.

Dependencies:
- eventbus v2.1 (internal) upgrade required; migration notes in docs.
- tokio-1.22 for concurrency primitives (service is Rust-based).
- Kafka routing-events topic for durability; ACLs may need updating.

Links to artifacts and context:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Event-Driven+Fallbacks+Design
- Incident replay dataset: gs://redwood-logs/incident-replays/2025-11-routing-spike.ldjson
- Implementation PR (work in progress): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4891
- Observability follow-up ticket: PM-4122 (hook fallback_event_latency to Console cost chart)

Customer impact: medium - this touches routing behavior. We will start on low-traffic canary to mitigate risk.

Security review required: false

2026-03-05 — Liam O'C: Implemented eventbus v2.1 integration and Kafka sink. Early canary harness is able to replay historical incident events against the coordinator. Pushed draft PR: /platform/pull/4891.
2026-03-09 — Observability (Ravi Patel): Added Grafana panels for fallback_event_latency_ms and added alert for convergence > 30s. Please wire fallback_audit_rate to the Console table before canary.

2026-03-11 — QA (Marisol Chen): Integration tests passed for optimistic CAS path. Noted a race in per-shard leases under heavy rebalance; added a mitigation to extend lease TTL by 50ms when rebalancing.
